question: My watch died and I am travelling. I wont be collecting data for a few days
answer: No problem. The dashboard will say "watch not synced" and the strip goes grey for those nights; no scores get logged, so nothing counts against the scoreboard. When it's charged again, open Garmin Connect once and the next pull backfills the gap automatically — nothing for you to do. Two things still worth doing without the watch: the evening check-in if you get a minute, and logging it if a migraine comes (tally.so/r/obWNYP?who=Garret). The attack log is the part that can't be backfilled.

question: Is the garmin the right tool for the job? Are there other technology products available that would help manage, give insight or predict the outcome?
answer:
Partly. For the one thing that holds up — sleep loss and schedule shifts — the Garmin is as good as anything: it gets bedtime, wake time and hours without you doing anything. Body Battery, stress and HRV are guesses; nobody has shown they predict attacks, and your own scoreboard so far is 13 scored days, one 9 (Oct 19) with no attack logged — a false alarm, no hits yet. Too early to call, but keep expectations low.

Alternatives: an Oura ring tracks sleep a bit better, same limits. Migraine Buddy is a diary, which you already have in the form. N1-Headache (formerly Curelator) is the one app with published trigger analysis; it needs about 90 days of daily entries before it says anything. Cefaly and Nerivio are treatment devices, not predictors — your prescriber's call. Nothing on the market predicts a migraine well. Your best predictor is you: prodrome signs in the evening check-in and how recently the last attack hit. Keep the watch for sleep; don't buy anything for prediction.
